cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel and son of David, has spent twenty years building the house of the LORD and his own palace. TWENTY YEARS, friend! I once left dough chilling so long it started getting mail, and that wasn't even CLOSE to twenty years.

cards.question: Hiram, king of Tyre (2 Chronicles 2:3), had given Solomon some cities. What does Solomon do with them?

answers.text: Rebuilds them and settles Israelites there
Hands them back to Hiram as a gift
Leaves them empty and falling apart

cards.text: Next, Solomon heads to a city called Hamath-zobah.

cards.question: When Solomon goes to Hamath-zobah, he captures it.

cards.text: Then Solomon builds Tadmor in the wilderness and store cities in Hamath, and rebuilds Upper and Lower Beth-horon as fortified cities with walls, gates and bars. Add Baalath, more store cities, and cities for his chariots and horses: whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon and all through his land. Me? I fold ONE cookie box and I need a nap.

cards.question: Some people are still left in the land from the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, and they're not Israelites. What does Solomon do with them?

answers.text: Sends them out of the land
Gives them land of their own

cards.question: Solomon doesn't put any of the Israelites to slave labor. What are the Israelites to him instead?

answers.text: His men of war and commanders

cards.text: The Israelites are also King Solomon's chief officers: 250 supervisors. My whole bakery has ONE supervisor, and it's the oven timer yelling at me every eleven minutes.
Then Solomon brings his wife, the daughter of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, up from the City of David. He moves her into a palace he had built for her.

cards.question: Solomon says his wife, Pharaoh's daughter, must not live in the house of David. Why not?

answers.text: The places the ark has entered are holy
The house of David belongs to the priests
The house of David is too small for her

cards.text: At that time, Solomon offers burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar he built in front of the portico. Cities, chariots, palaces, a whole kingdom to run, and the man STILL stops to worship the LORD.
He follows the daily requirement for offerings, just as Moses, Israel's leader, commanded, for Sabbaths, New Moons and the three yearly feasts: Unleavened Bread, Weeks and Tabernacles.

Next, Solomon sets up the temple crew: priests in divisions over their service, Levites to offer praise and minister before the priests, and gatekeepers by divisions at each gate. That's not just a temple anymore, friend, that's a WORK SCHEDULE.

cards.question: Solomon sets up the priests, Levites and gatekeepers by a new plan of his own, apart from anything David had commanded.
How closely is King Solomon's command about the priests and the Levites followed?

answers.text: Without turning aside in any matter
In every matter except the treasuries
Only in matters on the feast days

cards.question: From the day the foundation was laid, all of Solomon's work is carried out until the house of the LORD is completed.

cards.text: Then Solomon goes to Ezion-geber and Eloth, on the coast of Edom. Twenty years of building, and NOW the man goes to the coast.

cards.question: Out on the coast of Edom, who sends Solomon ships and crews of experienced sailors?
Hiram's sailors go with Solomon's servants to Ophir and bring back ___ for King Solomon.

cards.text: They deliver 450 talents of gold to King Solomon. FOUR HUNDRED FIFTY! The fanciest thing in the junk drawer I used to live in was a coupon that expired years ago.
